# Adrian Treleaven

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008)</sub>
- **Origin:** Ontario, Canada  <sub>[v4 c23 P11](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0011)</sub>
- **Role:** Journalist and author  <sub>[v4 c22 P20](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0020), [v4 c23 P19](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0019)</sub>

## Appearance

Adrian is a tall, broad-shouldered, handsome man. He has thick brown hair, a sharp nose and chin, and large, dark-gray eyes with a luminous, expressive quality. When smiling, he reveals an attractive set of white teeth, though his face otherwise carries a somewhat sorrowful and distracted expression.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010), [v4 c23 P28](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0028)_

## Personality

Adrian possesses a charming, witty, and passionate nature with a deep appreciation for beauty, poetry, and storytelling. He is sensitive, emotional, and possesses a strong capacity for empathy, often expressing his feelings with intense sincerity. Despite his romantic nature, he is guided by a sense of honor and duty in difficult emotional situations.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P28](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0028), [v4 c24 P15](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0015), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P10](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0010), [v4 c26 P24](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0024)_

- Write a major Canadian novel based on inspiring historical material  <sub>[v4 c23 P19](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0019), [v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)</sub>

## History

Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls Harbor in the summer to recuperate at Lorna Vane's home following a bout of typhoid fever and to visit the ancestral homestead built by his grandfather, John Tremayne. Upon meeting Captain Saul, Adrian was introduced to the captain's written logbook and agreed to collaborate on adapting his life story into a novel. During the summer, he spent his mornings writing at the lighthouse and his afternoons exploring the coast with Lorna, Nell, and Hugh Carrow. In the process, he fell deeply in love with Lorna Vane, though he kept his feelings secret out of respect for her situation regarding her husband, Rufus. Before departing Seven Gulls in the autumn to return to Toronto, he confessed his heartbreak to Nell. He later successfully published the novel based on Captain Saul's life, which achieved widespread critical and commercial success.

_Sources: [v4 c22 P20](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0020), [v4 c23 P11](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0011), [v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c25 P8](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0008), [v4 c25 P11](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0011), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P5](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0005), [v4 c26 P10](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0010), [v4 c35 P0](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Grandson of John Tremayne and Damaris Leigh, the original occupants of the house of dreams  <sub>[v4 c22 P20](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0020), [v4 c23 P11](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0011), [v4 c24 P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021)</sub>
- Son of Alice Tremayne, who passed away during his childhood  <sub>[v4 c24 P24](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0024), [v4 c24 P25](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0025)</sub>
- Nephew of Aunt Euphemia  <sub>[v4 c22 P20](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0020)</sub>
- Suffered from a severe attack of typhoid fever prior to visiting Seven Gulls  <sub>[v4 c22 P20](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0020)</sub>

## Quotes

> You cannot realize how delighted I am to be here, Mrs. Carrow. I have a strange sensation of returning home.  <sub>[v4 c23 P11](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0011)</sub>

> Lorna is loved by me, Mrs. Carrow. LOVED! A word that faint hardly seems sufficient!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>

> I was unable to prevent myself from loving her—that is everything—and my agony exceeds what I am capable of bearing.  <sub>[v4 c26 P5](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0005)</sub>

> And I will tread it—there is no need for you to doubt that I shall, Mrs. Carrow. Yet treading on glowing hot ploughshares would be less difficult.  <sub>[v4 c26 P10](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0010)</sub>

> Loving her and parting from her causes a scorching, searing agony—yet never having loved her remains completely unimaginable.  <sub>[v4 c26 P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018)</sub>
